articles.title: Newcastle transfer news: Nico Gonzalez completes £50m move from Man City
articles.summary: Nico Gonzalez joined Man City from Porto in February 2025 and played 59 times; the deal to take him to Newcastle is set to reach £50m after add-ons; the 24-year-old is Newcastle's seventh signing of the summer
articles.body:
The deal for the 24-year-old midfielder is set to reach £50m after add-ons. He will wear the No 6 shirt at St James' Park.

The midfielder said his goodbyes to his City team-mates on Tuesday morning before travelling to Newcastle and completed a medical on Wednesday, before he was presented to the club's fans ahead of their Carabao Cup clash with West Brom.

The Spaniard has become Matthias Jaissle's second signing as Magpies head coach after Amar Dedic joined last week.

Former Spain U21 international Gonzalez joined City from Porto in February 2025 and played 59 times for the club, scoring four goals.

Newcastle sporting director Ross Wilson said Gonzalez had been the Magpies' primary target, in a summer where they have lost Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali to Arsenal and Tottenham, given his experience already with Barcelona, Porto and in the Premier League with Manchester City.

He said: "We've worked patiently on this transfer for a number of weeks. This was the one we wanted, and we're delighted to welcome Nico to Newcastle United this evening. He was an ambitious target but following our discussions, he was so keen to join this club.

"He fits the exact criteria we set for this position and we weren't prepared to compromise on that. He's 24 years old, with an abundance of elite experience across Manchester City, FC Porto and Barcelona. He's already already shown his quality in the Premier League and we're sure there is more to come here in a black and white shirt."

articles.title: Celta - Osasuna | Rueda abre una grieta en el Celta: previa, análisis, pronóstico y predicción
articles.standfirst: Gallegos y navarros buscan su primera victoria en esta liga
articles.summary: Gallegos y navarros buscan su primera victoria en esta liga
articles.body: A pocos días del cierre del mercado, la incertidumbre por las posibles salidas y llegadas marcan la previa del partido en Balaídos. Si bien Osasuna parece tener configurada su plantilla, en el equipo gallego faltan flecos y hay asuntos pendientes, como el de Javi Rueda. La mejora salarial al jugador y el mensaje entre líneas de Giráldez evidencian un pequeño desencuentro en el club gallego, que busca centrarse tras una semana convulsa. Se ha hablando mucho más en las últimas horas del mercado y de esa posible salida de Javi Rueda que del partido ante Osasuna. Eso es lo que no quiere Claudio Giráldez que, pese a reclamar su continuidad en la rueda de prensa previa al partido, pidió que la atención se centre en el partido ante los navarros. El club rechazó por la tarde la oferta del Forest y formaliza una mejora del sueldo del carrilero para evitar su marcha. A excepción de la baja de Borja Iglesias, el técnico repite la convocatoria del pasado sábado en Mestalla y en la que se encuentra Javi Rueda, que además apunta a la titularidad. La primera jornada de liga, aplazada en este caso, aguarda mientras Osasuna trata de encontrar una buena versión. Tras empatar sin goles en casa ante el Levante, el cuadro dirigido por Luis Miguel Ramis visita Vigo con la idea de poder anotar por primera vez en el curso y llevarse los tres puntos. Todo ello, además, tratando de mejorar las sensaciones del estreno liguero en El Sadar, donde los rojillos estuvieron lejos de su mejor versión. Febas vs. Iker Muñoz. Sin Borja ni Budimir, a priori suplente, las miradas se centran en el mediocampo, donde el Celta tiene puestas muchas esperanzas en la llegada de Febas, llamado a marcar el ritmo de juego celeste. Algo similar ocurre con Iker Muñoz, al que muchos ven como el elegido para gobernar el mediocampo rojillo en los próximos años.

articles.title: Owono ficha por el Andorra
articles.standfirst: El Alavés ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Andorra laga el traspaso del guardameta guineano
articles.summary: El Alavés ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Andorra laga el traspaso del guardameta guineano
articles.body: Jesus Owono y el Alavés separan sus caminos. El conjunto gasteiztarra ha llegado a un acuerdo con el Andorra para traspasar al guardameta, que tras militar como cedido la pasada temporada en el conjunto andorrano, ahora regresa para hacerlo en propiedad. El fichaje se ha cerrado a coste cero y el ecuatoguineano podría estrenarse este domingo ante el Eibar. La salida de Owono estaba decidida desde que Quique se decantó por Adrián Rodríguez como pareja de baile de Antonio Sivera bajo palos. El técnico madrileño quería examinar durante la pretemporada a los dos guardametas que estuvieron cedidos en Segunda y finalmente se decantó por la continuidad del ex del Real Zaragoza, que trabajará junto al propio Sivera y Swiderski. Owono pone fin a una trayectoria de casi una década como babazorro. Aterrizó en Vitoria con 16 años para recalar en las categorías inferiores del club y fue escalando hasta dar el salto al primer equipo, donde ha disputado 20 partidos (12 de Liga y 8 de Copa del Rey). A la sombra de Sivera desde su aparición al primer equipo, el club decidió cederle la pasada temporada al Andorra para que tuviera minutos y ahora regresa al Principado en propiedad. El Alavés le ha agradecido los servicios prestados y le desea lo mejor en su futuro. El Deportivo Alavés y el FC Andorra han alcanzado un acuerdo para el traspaso de Jesús Owono, que emprende una nueva etapa profesional tras una larga trayectoria ligada a la entidad albiazul. El guardameta llegó a la cantera del Deportivo Alavés con 16 años y desde entonces fue creciendo dentro de la estructura alavesista hasta alcanzar el primer equipo, debutar con la camiseta albiazul y defender la portería del Deportivo Alavés en la máxima categoría. Ahora, el guardameta internacional con Guinea Ecuatorial cierra su etapa como albiazul y emprende un nuevo reto en su carrera de la mano del FC Andorra. El Deportivo Alavés quiere agradecer a Jesús Owono su dedicación, profesionalidad y compromiso durante todos estos años y desearle la mayor de las suertes, tanto en esta nueva etapa como en los retos que le depare el futuro.

articles.title: 'Infarto' del Hearts para amarrar la Conference
articles.standfirst: Se impusieron al Rapid Viena en penaltis tras haber caído previamente de Champions y Europa League
articles.summary: Se impusieron al Rapid Viena en penaltis tras haber caído previamente de Champions y Europa League
articles.body: El fútbol ha sido demasiado duro durante los últimos meses con el Hearts. Pero, al menos, se conformarán con disputar la próxima edición de la Conference League tras imponerse al Rapid Viena de Demir, ex del Barcelona, por penaltis (2(3)-(4)-2) No hace muchos meses, se quedaron a un partido de poner fin al eterno duopolio de Celtic y Rangers en Escocia. Perdieron, además, Lawrence Shankland, uno de sus mejores jugadores, y arrancaron la Champions League desde la segunda ronda previa... donde el Sturm Graz les pasó por encima. Descendidos a la Europa League, el destino les juntó con un Benfica que tampoco tuvo piedad alguna y dejó la eliminatoria sentenciada en el partido de ida disputado en Lisboa. La Conference pasó a ser la última bala para jugar en Europa esta temporada y les tocó contra el Rapid de Viena. El empate rescatado en el duelo de ida disputado en Edimburgo complicó más todavía si cabe la misión. Lo peor, sin embargo, llegaría a los 34' del partido de vuelta con el tanto de Ercan Kara que mandó al Rapid por delante al descanso. Lograron forzar la prórroga tras quedarse con uno menos y, en el tiempo 'extra', Calvin Miller anotó el 1-2. articles.title: Nicolas Jackson transfer news: Villa close to £65m move for Chelsea forward
articles.summary: The striker is nearing a move to Villa Park after three years at Chelsea.
articles.body:
Aston Villa are close to an agreement to sign striker Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea in a deal worth up to £65m.

There is a broad agreement between the clubs over the terms of a move for the 25-year-old, with Chelsea set to achieve their asking price with an initial sum of £47.5m with £17.5m in add-ons.

And if the Senegal international agrees personal terms and completes the switch to Villa his arrival is likely to trigger England international Ollie Watkins' move to Saudi Pro League side Al-Hilal.

The deal remains subject to personal terms being agreed, but negotiations are at an advanced stage, with Jackson expected to reunite with Unai Emery having played under the Villa boss at Spanish club Villarreal.

Jackson would become the latest player in Villa's summer rebuild following the arrivals of record buy Johan Manzambi, midfielder Joao Gomes, goalkeeper Zion Suzuki and defender Matteo Ruggeri.

However, there has also been significant movement out of the club and Watkins leaving would mean they had sold five of the starting XI who won the Europa League in May.

Morgan Rogers , Youri Tielemans, Lucas Digne and Ezri Konsa have already left with goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez expected to depart too.

Chelsea are weighing up a move for the Argentine, who is now deemed surplus to requirements after Suzuki joined from Parma.

In signing Jackson, Villa would be getting a forward who joined Chelsea from Villarreal for £35m in 2023 and scored 30 goals in 81 appearances.

His most recent appearance for the Blues came against Fluminense in the Club World Cup in 2025, while he also won the Europa Conference League with the club.

He spent last season on loan to Bayern Munich, scoring 11 times in 34 games and helping Bayern win the Bundesliga.

Chelsea banked a £14.3m loan fee from the move, though an obligation to buy for £56.2m was not triggered after Jackson failed to make 40 appearances of 45 minutes or more.

Fellow forward Liam Delap is also likely to leave the Blues, with a £50m fee agreed with Nottingham Forest for the striker.

Meanwhile, the club have also been holding talks with Atalanta's Honest Ahanor, 18, over a potential move to Stamford Bridge. The defender is valued at £34.3m by the Italian club.

articles.title: Southern Miss football no longer hosting Mississippi State in 2030 schedule
articles.summary: Southern Miss football will no longer be hosting Mississippi State in Hattiesburg for a nonconference game in 2030.
articles.body:
Southern Miss football will no longer be hosting Mississippi State for a 2030 nonconference game, a Southern Miss program spokesperson confirmed to the Clarion Ledger on Aug. 26.

It was part of a home-and-home series with the Golden Eagles making a return trip to in Starkville in 2031. Instead, they will now play just one game in 2029 at Davis Wade Stadium.

Neither program has commented on why the games were canceled, including dropping Southern Miss' home game, when contacted by the Clarion Ledger.

The news comes though as Mississippi State begins a nine-game SEC schedule in 2026 that has led to canceled nonconference games. The Bulldogs did the same for Memphis with two future games canceled . The contract for that series did not require a buyout because of the SEC's nine-game schedule.

Southern Miss has one other nonconference game scheduled for 2029 at UConn . It has two 2030 nonconference games scheduled against Middle Tennessee State and Memphis, but no 2031 games scheduled because Louisiana Tech is now part of the Sun Belt Conference.

Mississippi State has one other 2029 nonconference game against West Georgia and one 2030 game against Troy. Both games are at Davis Wade Stadium.

The Bulldogs defeated the Golden Eagles, 34-17, in the 2025 season opener at M. M. Roberts Stadium, which was recently renamed to Renasant Stadium.

articles.title: TCU football pulls reporter credential after assault story
articles.summary: The Star-Telegram said its access to covering the TCU football team has been rescinded after its reporting of an alleged assault in the locker room.
articles.body:
TCU pulled the credentials of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram following the newspaper's reporting of an assault that took place in the football team's locker room.

The Star-Telegram revealed its access to the team was rescinded on Wednesday, Aug. 26, saying that the school made the decision due to the victim of the assault allegedly receiving threats of the news.

"The Star-Telegram did not identify the player, junior wide receiver Dozie Ezukanma, until three days after the initial report, when he identified himself in a now-deleted Instagram video," the Star-Telegram said in a statement.

TCU athletic director Mike Buddie defended the decision, saying in a statement the school's focus is the health and wellbeing of our student athlete.

"Unfortunately, an unnamed source without first-hand knowledge of the incident provided inaccurate information cited in initial reporting by the Fort Worth Star-Telegram, which we strongly disputed," Buddie said. "The inclusion of the misinformation advanced a narrative that endangered a student-athlete and resulted in threats to him and his family. These actions led to the decision to withhold the media credential until additional conversation can be held between athletics and the sports reporting team. We remain dedicated to restoring our student to health as well as focusing on the game that's ahead."

The Star-Telegram said TCU did not specify what would need to be done to gain access back. The decision comes less than a week before the Horned Frogs open the football season against North Carolina in Dublin, Ireland, on Saturday, Aug. 29. The publication noted its beat writer is traveling to the game, and his credential for it was revoked since TCU is the designated home team, therefore it can determine who is credentialed.

Ranking colleges with largest stadiums based on tuition

What incident led to TCU revoking credentials?

The episode began with the Star-Telegram's report on Aug. 18 after safety Jacob Fields was dismissed from the program from what TCU said was "a violation of team rules."

The story from the newspaper reported Fields got into an altercation with an offensive player and allegedly struck a him. The incident led to a TCU football staffer contacting campus police that was listed as an aggravated assault that "occurred in the men's locker room" that took place on Aug. 13 at 1:30 p.m., according to a police report. The staffer's statement was redacted from the report, but included the responding officer told the member to have the victim contact police for more information into an investigation and possibly filing charges.

"This is an ongoing investigation, and we are limited in what information we can release at this time," TCU chief of police Robert Rangel said in a statement to USA TODAY Sports.

While the Star-Telegram did not name the victim, junior wide receiver Dozie Ezukanma identified himself in a now-deleted Instagram video he was the person that was involved in the incident, which led TCU to its decision.

The Star-Telegram noted it is the only media outlet that covers TCU athletics on a full-time basis, including beat writers, photographers and columnists.

Shehan Jeyarajah, the president of the Football Writers Association of America, condemned the decision on social media .

"I strongly disagree with TCU's decision to ban the Star-Telegram from coverage," he wrote. "Steven Johnson has covered TCU with class for years and his credential to cover the game in Ireland should be reinstated immediately."

articles.title: QBs to start in SEC as true freshman: Tennessee's Faizon Brandon joins short list including Peyton Manning
articles.summary: The Sporting News takes a look at some SEC quarterbacks who emerged as starters during their true freshman season.
articles.body:
Billed as college football's greatest conference, the SEC is hardly for the youth. True freshmen have undoubtedly made an impact in the superconference. Harold Perkins Jr. , LaRon Landry and Herschel Walker all found success during their maiden campaigns.

And yet, true freshman quarterbacks have tended to watch from the sidelines when they arrive on campus, biding their time in the shadows as more experienced talents take aim inside the pocket.

Conventional wisdom would suggest this is a smart strategy. The SEC is a gauntlet that can wreak havoc on players unfamiliar with its pace, physicality and tactics. The difference between a first-year player and a redshirt senior can feel like an ocean-sized gulf.

Still, as the old adage goes, if you're good enough, you're old enough. The spotlight wasn't too big for a select few SEC newcomers, who rose through the ranks to establish themselves as SEC heavyweights in their maiden campaigns.

With that, here's a look at some notable SEC quarterbacks who emerged as starters during their true freshman seasons.

Notable QBs to start in SEC as true freshman

A gifted talent from Mathews, Louisiana, Hodson was one of college football's finest talents during his maiden season in Baton Rouge in 1986. The then-teenager was named first team All-SEC setting conference records for the passing yards (2,261) and passing touchdowns (19) by a freshman.

Fueled by his displays, the Tigers claimed their first SEC title in 16 years. His performances that season set the stage for a splendid career that saw Hodson become the first SEC hurler to surpass 8,000 passing yards and 60 passing touchdowns.

Having come of age on the gridiron in an unusual place — Zeier went to high school in Germany — the famed Bulldog gunslinger swiftly made a name for himself in Athens.

Zeier started the 1991 season as a backup. He was inserted into Ray Goff's lineup for its Oct. 5 tilt against No. 6 Clemson. The Bulldogs downed the heavily favored Tigers, 27-12, with Zeier throwing for two touchdowns. He wouldn't relinquish his position, starting each of the next 40 games for Georgia.

The Bulldogs won seven of their next nine games, with Zeier tallying 1,984 yards and seven touchdowns. He would become Georgia's most decorated passer by the time he left campus, finishing his career with more passing yards than any other SEC quarterback. Zeier placed seventh in Heisman voting in his senior season. He was elected to the Georgia Sports Hall of Fame in 2022.

Taneyhill was a precocious talent out of high school. He knew as much, reportedly issuing the following message to then-South Carolina boss Sparky Woods before his maiden year: "Start me and we win."

The Gamecocks star did a lot of winning in his maiden season. Taneyhill had to bide his time in the shadows during the 1994 season, watching from the sidelines as South Carolina dropped its opening five games. Woods eventually gave him his chance, handing him the reins to the Gamecocks' offense.

His decision was an inspired one. Taneyhill tallied 1,272 yards and seven touchdowns as South Carolina won five of its final six games.

The teenager was named National Freshman of the Year by Sports Illustrated for his heroics. He went on to collect nearly 9,000 yards and 62 touchdowns during his time in Columbia. He was inducted into South Carolina's Hall of Fame in 2006.

A highly touted prospect out of nearby Fort Walton Beach, Fla., Wuerffel quickly surged to the top of Steve Spurrier's QB depth chart. The College Football Hall of Famer found success in Spurrier's "Fun 'n' Gun" system, amassing 2,230 yards and 22 touchdowns as the Gators climbed as high as No. 4 in the AP rankings.

The Gators capped off their season with a 41-7 blowout win over No. 3 West Virginia in the Sugar Bowl. Wuerffel earned SEC Freshman of the Year honors for his displays. Three years later, he'd add to his collection of career accomplishments, landing the Heisman Trophy while leading Florida to its first national championship.

Odds are, you have heard Manning's name before. Before he was making waves as a record-breaking gunslinger in the NFL, Manning was arguably one of college football's greatest-ever quarterbacks.

Some were surprised Manning spurned his father's alma mater, Ole Miss, for Tennessee. He didn't figure to factor into the Volunteers' plans as a freshman, starting the 1994 season as the team's third-string quarterback.

Injuries wracked the Volunteers' QB room. Manning served as the understudy to Todd Helton (yes, that Todd Helton) before replacing him after Helton suffered a knee injury. Suffice to say, Manning didn't surrender his place in Phillip Fulmer's offense, leading the Vols to wins in seven of their last eight games.

Manning's freshman-year figures didn't quite reach the heights of his following three campaigns. But 1,141 yards and 11 touchdowns to six interceptions is nothing to sniff at for a first-year passer who entered the year at the bottom of the depth chart.

Leak recorded 2,435 yards and 16 touchdowns to 11 interceptions during his true freshman season in 2003. Named a five-star prospect during his time at Independence High School (North Carolina), Leak showed flashes of brilliance during his maiden year in Gainesville. The then-teenager steered the Gators to wins over eventual national champion LSU as well as No. 4 Georgia in that famous 2003 season, offering flits of light to a fairly dour campaign in Ron Zook's final year as head coach. MORE : Tracking which pro players are returning to college football

Hurts made history shortly after arriving on campus in Tuscaloosa, becoming the first true freshman to be named starting quarterback since Vince Sutton in 1984.

He went on to shatter Alabama's record books during his first year, setting the record for most rushing yards (954) and most rushing touchdowns (13) for a Crimson Tide passer. He finished the year with 36 total touchdowns, another program record.

Fueled by Hurts' heroics, Alabama surged to the national title game. The Crimson Tide fell in the national championship game to Clemson. Still, Hurts' displays proved dazzling — he landed SEC Freshman and SEC Offensive Player of the Year honors.

Like many of the names on this list, Fromm entered his freshman year as an understudy, wearing the headset as Jacob Eason took snaps to start the 2017 season. Eason was cut down in Georgia's first game, prompting Fromm to surge to the top of Mark Richt's QB depth chart.

Fromm finished his maiden season with 2,615 yards and 24 touchdowns to just seven interceptions. The Bulldogs posted a 12-2 record under Fromm's watch before falling in the national championship game to Alabama.

Nix was named Auburn's starting quarterback ahead of the 2019 season. A four-star prospect out of Alabama, the teenager performed admirably for the 9-4 Tigers, tallying 16 touchdowns and six interceptions en route to SEC Freshman of the Year honors.

His most impactful showcase came in the Iron Bowl against the Crimson Tide. Nix accounted for more than 200 yards of total offense and two touchdowns as Auburn downed its hated rival in their regular-season finale.

© Brianna Paciorka/News Sentinel / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images

Brandon is the latest true freshman to take hold of his team's starting lineup, landing the staring nod in Josh Heupel's setup ahead of the 2026 season. A consensus five-star prospect, the Greensboro, North Carolina native takes over for former Appalachian State star Joey Aguilar. He'll guide a veteran-laden attack that features eight returning starters, including 1,000-yard back DeSean Bishop and former five-star Mike Matthews, who tallied 53 catches for 853 yards as a sophomore last year.

articles.title: Texas Tech football adds Florida State QB out of transfer portal

Joey McGuire wasn't lying when he said he was open to adding more pieces to the Texas Tech football team for the 2026 season.

articles.title: ESPN Replaces Lead ‘College GameDay’ Producer in Shakeup
articles.summary: It marks the show’s second EP change in three years.
articles.body:
On the eve of the new college football season, ESPN is shaking up production leadership on College GameDay , Front Office Sports has confirmed.

Producer Jim Gaiero is being transferred into a broader role across ESPN's live events portfolio, sources say. Matthew Garrett, Gaiero's boss for the past three years as vice president of production, is taking over as executive producer of the venerable college football pregame show. His previous roles include serving as coordinating producer of Sunday NFL Countdown and Monday Night Countdown .

Awful Announcing broke the news of GameDay 's producer change .

Gaiero led GameDay for the past 10 years—a period of major cast changes that included the addition of Pat McAfee and Nick Saban, the departure of David Pollack, and the retirement of Lee Corso.

With the sports media giant going all-out for its first-ever Super Bowl telecast, Gaiero, a 31-year ESPN veteran, is expected to produce pregame and related programming around ESPN/ABC's simulcast of Super Bowl LXI on Feb. 14, 2027. Gaiero will also continue to produce college football games.

Mike McQuade, ESPN's executive vice president of sports production, is also expected to employ Gaiero on Masters and PGA Championship golf coverage, with an eye toward him assuming full production responsibilities in 2028.

It's the second time in three years that ESPN has shaken up production leadership around the 40-year-old GameDay . In August 2023, ESPN parted ways with star producer Lee Fitting, who now serves as head of media and production for WWE.

As for Garrett, the 21-year ESPN veteran has been a vocal supporter of McAfee's in recent years. In a 2024 interview with Sports Business Journal , Garrett referred to the West Virginia product as "a unique talent," while praising his "incredible ability for engaging the on-site crowd."

"If you ask me, it's unmatched by anybody else on television," he said of McAfee.

The surprise GameDay leadership switch will inevitably lead to soap opera-like speculation about what role McAfee played, if any, behind the scenes.

There's no question that the addition of McAfee in 2022 and Saban in 2024 has revitalized the iconic show. GameDay is coming off its most-watched season ever, averaging 2.7 million viewers in 2025, a 22% increase. Led by Corso's Week 1 farewell, the show posted its nine most-watched regular-season episodes ever last season.

But the mercurial, 39-year-old McAfee has also butted heads with GameDay colleagues and ESPN executives, mocking them as "old white people." Last year, FOS reported that some co-workers were fed up with McAfee's "diva-like" behavior. McAfee previously lashed out at powerful former ESPN executive Norby Williamson as a "rat" trying to sabotage his show.

Meanwhile, McAfee's ESPN portfolio continues to grow, including joining the cast of the Monday Night Countdown NFL pregame show this season and likely hosting his own "Field Pass" of Super Bowl LXI. The former NFL punter has the support of ESPN's most powerful executives. They include: chairman Jimmy Pitaro; president of content Burke Magnus; and Mike Foss, the increasingly influential executive vice president, executive editor of sports news and entertainment, who serves as McAfee's liaison.

Even McAfee GameDay castmates would admit he's now the show's biggest star. His weekly field goal contest, in which he's generously given away $6 million of his own money, has become must-see TV. When ESPN issued its press release touting GameDay's upcoming season, McAfee was conspicuously pictured front and center alongside Herbstreit, Saban, and Davis.

In July, FOS first reported that McAfee had begun early talks on a long-term contract extension , worth an estimated $60 million a year . While McAfee licenses his eponymous weekday show to ESPN, he has a separate deal for GameDay . His current ESPN deals are set to expire in 2028.

Meanwhile, ESPN's top execs are said to be thrilled at GameDay's newfound ability to reach both younger (under 25) and female viewers. Audiences in those two key advertising-desired demos grew 35% and 34% last season, respectively. GameDay's ratings grew 23% last year and would have still increased by 12% without the bump it received from Nielsen's Big Data measurement system.

This season's nine-person GameDay cast of McAfee, Saban, Herbstreit, Davis, Desmond Howard, "Stanford Steve" Coughlin, Jen Lada, Jess Sims, and Pete Thamel is poised to kick off the new season with a trip to Baton Rouge, Louisiana, in Week 1. The telecast will mark GameDay's 500th road show. This will be Herbstreit's 30th season on the show. In May, the GameDay team won its third consecutive Sports Emmy for outstanding weekly sports studio program.

articles.title: Who Barcelona Want to Play and Avoid in the Champions League Draw
articles.summary: The draw for the league phase will be made on Thursday.
articles.body:
Barcelona will discover who they will face in the league phase of the 2026-27 Champions League when the draw is made in Monaco on Thursday, August 27 th . The full list of teams and Pots can be found right here .

The Catalans will be hoping for a kind draw but the competition's new format means there are likely to be at least a few tasty ties for Hansi Flick's side to contend with over the next few months.

With the competition coming after a busy summer for many players, Barca would surely prefer to avoid any trips to far-flung places, while also saving the biggest names until 2027 when the business end of the competition rolls around.

Barca will be in Pot 1 for the draw along with the highest ranked teams. However, the Catalans can't play La Liga rivals Real Madrid and Atletico due to country protection and there are a few more sides they will want to avoid.

The prospect of facing Luis Enrique and PSG again is enticing, particularly the chance to come up against Ferran Torres and Dro Fernandez , but Barcelona would probably rather avoid taking on the defending champions so early on in the competition.

Last season's beaten finalists Arsenal and Bundesliga champions Bayern Munich may also be best saved until later but Barcelona will fancy the remaining teams in Pot 1.

Manchester City and Liverpool are both under new management heading into the new season, with Enzo Maresca having taken charge of the Cityzens and Andoni Iraola replacing Arne Slot at Anfield.

If there's ever a good time to face either Premier League club, it may just be right now. Barca will also fancy taking on Inter and gaining revenge for their semi-final defeat at the hands of the Nerazzurri back in 2024-25.

Pot 2 contains more Premier League teams and Barcelona may just relish a glamour tie with Manchester United and the chance for a swift reunion with Marcus Rashford .

The Red Devils are back in the competition after Michael Carrick revived their fortunes last season and pulled off an impressive third-placed finish. However, that's been followed by a quietish summer in the transfer window and an opening day defeat to Hull City that hardly inspires confidence for the season ahead.

Europa League winners Aston Villa may also hold few fears for Barcelona. Unai Emery's side have sold Morgan Rogers , Ezri Konsa and Youri Tielemans this summer and may lose a few more key players before the transfer window closes in Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez .

Barcelona will also be happy to be paired with Dortmund , Club Brugge or PSV again. The Catalans have enjoyed wins over all three teams in recent seasons in the Champions League and will feel confident if drawn against them again.

If there's one team that may give Barcelona nightmares it could be Roma. A trip to Italy would bring back memories of the 2018 collapse when Ernesto Valverde's side threw away a 3-0 lead in the Italian capital and crashed out.

Pots 3 and 4 are still yet to be fully confirmed but already contain some new faces and potentially intriguing encounters to look out for in Thursday's draw.

Former Barcelona star Cesc Fabregas has led Como into the competition for the first time in their history and the Serie A side will be desperate to make a mark in the tournament in their debut campaign. Como may therefore prove to be tricky opponents along with Lens. The Ligue 1 side pushed PSG all the way in France last season and are no pushovers.

Victor Osimhen 's Galatasaray are another team likely to cause problems. The Turkish side beat Liverpool home and away last season and Barca will know that Istanbul is never an easy place to go in the Champions League. A trip to the Arctic Circle to face Bodo/Glimt may also be one to avoid along with an away trip to Azerbaijan to face Sabah.

Elsewhere, Feyenoord and Lille will hold few fears for Barcelona, along with teams such as LASK, Stuttgart and Slavia Prague.

Who would you like to see Barcelona face in the Champions League and which teams are best avoided? Share your thoughts, opinions and answers in the comments section below!

articles.title: USA TODAY Sports predicts the Oklahoma Sooners record for 2026
articles.summary: What will the Oklahoma Sooners record be in 2026? USA TODAY Sports makes their prediction.
articles.body:
Around the country, a number of outlets have high expectations for the Oklahoma Sooners . This comes on the heels of a 10-2 season and a College Football Playoff appearance in 2025. The Sooners were No. 7 in USA TODAY Sports' 1-138 rankings released earlier this week.

In their record predictions for the 2026 season, USA TODAY Sports college football analysts Paul Myerberg and Ramon Padilla predicted Oklahoma to go 10-2 once again. The duo didn't share which games Oklahoma loses, but they probably have Oklahoma losing to Texas and Georgia.

That seems right about where most prognosticators are landing with the Sooners, give or take a game or two. Given the Sooners' schedule, the floor looks like it could be 8-4. As crazy as it would sound, undefeated is on the table. The Sooners haven't gone undefeated during the regular season since 2004. That's not to say they can't. Simply that it's a long shot.

But back in the playoff is right where Oklahoma needs to be if they want to contend for a national title. 10-2 would mean the Sooners would have to win four games to win the national title. Not unprecedented. Ohio State did it back in 2024.

The Oklahoma Sooners have an opportunity to do some big things this season. Especially if they can get the running game going. That's been the focus this offseason, and by all accounts, it looks better than it did a year ago. If that turns out to be the case, the Sooners will be one of the best teams in college football.

articles.title: Wouter Vrancken's side come of age as Hearts bid goodnight Rapid Vienna
articles.summary: After some early season setbacks, "proud" Wouter Vrancken believes Hearts are getting their rewards by securing Conference League progress.
articles.body:
If 16 May was the day the dream ended, 26 August may well turn out to be when the next one started for Hearts.

A mere three months on from a final-day defeat that denied Hearts a first Scottish top-flight title in 66 years, they have not only secured a tangible reward for finishing as runners-up, they did so with immense courage and togetherness.

Thursday's victory over Rapid Vienna on penalties secured a place in Friday's league phase draw for the Conference League and two games each in October, November and December.

A lot has changed in that three months - a new head coach in Belgian Wouter Vrancken, player departures and plenty arrivals - and a sticky start to the season threatened to prolong a sense of malaise after that 3-1 defeat by champions Celtic.

European and domestic losses got the 2026-27 campaign off to a whimper but Vrancken stayed calm and believes his team are now reaping deserved benefits.

"They have to learn that they're a good team, that they're good players, that they can show it," he told BBC Scotland.

"In the last away games in Europe, you see that they're a little bit scared to do things, to take risks or to give spaces away. Then we don't play our game.

"The development of the team, the progress of the team is amazing. The team spirit, I saw it from the first session already.

"They want to learn it. They wanted to have feedback. They want to go into it and the kind of football we played. This is the result. They get rewarded and I'm so happy for them."

Heroic Hearts beat Rapid Vienna on penalties to secure Conference League progress

Visit our Hearts page for all the latest news, analysis and fan views

While the margin of Hearts' 6-0 aggregate loss to Sturm Graz in the Champions League second qualifying round may have been unexpected, the result was not much of a surprise.

Even less surprising was losing to Benfica, typically a Champions League team, in the Europa League qualifiers, though again the margin was heavy at 7-1 on aggregate.

Facing Rapid Vienna in the Conference League play-off represented another tough tie, though not considered as tough as either Sturm Graz or Benfica.

Roughly this time last year, Dundee United took Rapid to penalties in their Conference League qualifying tie but lost in the shootout and the improvement in Hearts' domestic form after a losing start at Aberdeen raised hopes that European league phase football was achievable.

Hearts more than gave as good as they got in the first leg, but the absence of a lead to take over to Austria made Rapid slight favourites at 2-2, more so after Ercan Kara gave them a 1-0 lead on the night at the Allianz Stadion.

A Tomas Magnusson red card for Hearts preceded the Pierre Landry Kabore equaliser that forced extra time. Calvin Miller's volley very nearly secured them the win only for Nenad Cvetkovic to level for Rapid on 119 minutes.

A first save in the shootout from Beau Reus to deny Moulaye Haidara put Hearts within touching distance again but Oisin McEntee's spot-kick getting blocked prolonged the tension.

Up stepped Marco Tilio, a former Celtic winger perhaps with a point to prove after a frustrating spell in Glasgow. But it was Reus who had the last word with another terrific stop to secure a 4-3 win on penalties.

Vrancken's post-match comments revealed how much he believes his side have come in a short space of time.

"When you see the game, we played a really bad first half, a little bit similar as we did in Benfica," he explained.

"We made agreements, we had a game plan and we didn't follow up, we didn't show the guts to follow up.

"When you play against a side like Rapid Vienna, when you don't show it, they can play through you. We were already pretty angry at half-time and we came out, we did much better.

"We took the game in our hands, we were dominant at that moment. This is already a mental strength, coming back on 1-0 down and coming back like this.

"Again, in the extra time, you try to take the game with you to Hearts and to Edinburgh, then you get a mental kick again in the last minute of the extra time.

"Again, I'm so proud of these guys that they stay in the game, focused and concentrated to win the penalties.

"We can make more steps in the coming weeks and hope that we can take the steps as soon as possible."

Progress in Europe brings obvious financial rewards and there may be sales as well as purchases at Hearts in the closing days of the transfer window.

Hearts have already brought in 12 new players this summer while even more than that have moved on.

Now with at least six more European fixtures to play this season, former Hearts player Ryan Stevenson believes the club will have to recruit.

"I think they'll definitely need to bring in another two or three anyway when you look at the League Cup, the six games in Europe, the league, which is so important," he told BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound.

Another former Tynecastle favourite, Allan Preston, believes Hearts will be prepared for such a task.

"They've got people ready to come if they're needed," he said. "They are ready. They don't wait until things happen. They already do things.

"If they need to, they'll be pushing the button before the transfer window closes. They will get better, they'll produce better."

One position Hearts may have to look at as a priority is midfield after Tom Renaud's first-half injury.

"That's the biggest disappointment of the evening," lamented Vrancken.

"It's not looking good but I hope for him that it's OK. We have to look there because he was also really good in the last game.

"We're talking every day about those things and we'll see in the next weeks."

articles.title: Preston North End 0-4 Everton: Thierno Barry scores hat-trick as David Moyes' Toffees saunter into Carabao Cup third round
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second-round tie between Preston North End and Everton at Deepdale; Thierno Barry follows up his goal in the Premier League opener with a hat-trick and an assist to send the Toffees into third round
articles.body:
The French striker scored eight goals in 41 games in 2025/26 and, after his first of the season in Saturday's Premier League win over Crystal Palace, is now already halfway to matching that total despite having played 38 games fewer.

The Toffees - who have not progressed past the third round since 2023/24 - have been drawn to face Wolves in the next round.

Latest news and rumours: Everton | Watch FREE PL highlights

A strong Everton team were in control from the off. They dominated the ball and chances came thick and fast against a Preston side who've lost two from two in the Sky Bet Championship but, for the most part, those openings were of low quality.

The 10th attempt was a successful one. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall's floated ball released Vitalii Mykolenko on the left, who laid the ball on a plate for Barry to sweep in a tidy finish.

There was a feeling the floodgates might open after that, but they didn't, so when the second half began, Preston had the bit between their teeth, which the crowd sensed.

However, Barry's second just before the hour made the comeback less likely, and his simple finish to complete his hat-trick essentially secured Everton's progression with 20 minutes to play.

There was time for Brennan Johnson to add shine to the result, with the Welshman - who joined from Crystal Palace earlier this month - netting his first goal since November 2025 to make it 4-0.

25: GOAL ! After nine previous attempts, Barry finishes off a slick move to put Everton in front.

39: CHANCE ! Merlin Rohl gifts Preston a chance when he misjudges a bounce, allowing Delano Burgzorg to pull the ball back to Leo Leroy, who fires over from a promising position.

45: SAVE ! Great stop from North End debutant Lee Nicholls, who denies Tyler Dibling at his near post.

47: BLOCK ! James Tarkowski sticks a foot in to brilliantly turn away Delano Burgzorg's shot as Preston chase an equaliser.

59: GOAL ! Iliman Ndiaye tees up Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall, whose cross is pushed straight into the path of Barry, who makes no mistake.

65: SAVE ! Jordan Pickford makes his only significant save of the night to keep out a sweetly-struck overhead kick from Callum Lang.

70: GOAL ! Dewsbury-Hall finds substitute Johnson, who gains a yard on Lewis Gibson and squares for Barry, who sweeps in to complete his hat-trick.

72: GOAL ! Barry turns provider, laying a beautiful ball off for Johnson, who arrives in a similar position, but this time goes alone to add the gloss.

Heckingbottom: The second goal changed the game

Preston 's Paul Heckingbottom speaking on Sky Sports Football:

"It's just frustrating we were going to make the subs and they scored the (second) goal as we had them all lined up. It just changed the game. The goals after that were disappointing

"We were playing against top opposition, we know that, but one or two things, fundamentally, don't help you keep clean sheets anyway. It doesn't matter who you are playing against.

"Because of where we are at the minute, it's hard to take the pressure off the defenders as we've not got attacking changes. We've got defenders on the bench, a couple more midfielders, wing-backs and some young boys. That's where we're at; we need attacking changes so we can keep the pressure on. And that's a problem for us at the minute."

Moyes discusses progression, Barry and Johnson

Everton 's David Moyes speaking on Sky Sports Football:

"It ended up being a little bit more comfortable than I thought it might have been before the game, but it's a really good result for us.

"I thought we played well at times and our football was quite good, but we need to finish things off a bit better in the first half than we did, but I'm really pleased we scored four goals."

On Thierno Barry : "I told him [at the end of last season] he has to do a lot better than he did before. That's it. We want centre-forwards to score goals. I don't think it's easy for anybody coming to the Premier League in their first season, especially centre-forwards. He'll learn a lot more, he'll see a lot more and he's come in with a much better attitude generally, so whoever's working with him is doing a good job."

On Brennan Johnson : "We want to find what he did at Tottenham when he was scoring all those goals. His assist tonight was brilliant and his finish as well. People who've watched Brennan over the years will tell you that looks a bit more like him. We don't want to bring him on too quick, but he's done well tonight."

articles.title: Tottenham Hotspur 5-1 Charlton Athletic: Savio scores and assists on debut as Spurs ease into Carabao Cup third round
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup second-round tie between Tottenham Hotspur and Charlton Athletic at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium; new signing Savio made an immediate impact after coming off the bench to make his Spurs debut
articles.body:
The Brazilian, signed from Man City for £85m on Tuesday , was introduced as a second-half substitute and took just 11 minutes to open his account, adding to the hype surrounding his arrival in north London.

Roberto De Zerbi named a strong side to face the Championship opposition, with many senior names included in the starting XI after Spurs' dreadfully disappointing defeat to Brentford in their Premier League opener.

Latest news and rumours: Tottenham | Watch FREE PL highlights

It was youngster Mikey Moore who finally broke down a stubborn Charlton defence though, smashing the ball through the hands of Tiernan Brooks to score his first Tottenham goal. That lead was quickly doubled just five minutes later, with Dominic Solanke smartly finishing after the visitors failed to clear their lines.

Several other high profile names were introduced after an hour, including Kevin Danso who headed home from a Mateus Fernandes free-kick with his first touch. However, Spurs fans will only thinking about the magic of Savio after he came on in the 71st minute.

The forward cut inside from the right and fired smartly into the bottom corner to add Spurs' fourth, before his scrappy effort deflected off veteran Ben Davies for a fifth just three minutes later.

There was still time for Charlton to find a consolation courtesy of the head of Lloyd Jones, but it meant little as Spurs cruised into third round, where they will meet Liverpool at Anfield .

'He lit the place up' - All the reaction from Savio's electric Spurs start

"He lit the place up. This is what Tottenham want. Players like that who can get you off your seat. Who can cut inside and hit a ferocious left footed shot. He was excellent."

"When players are full of confidence, especially attacking players, they like to attack at you. He's no different. The confidence is there to be seen."

"He did great when he came on. He's going to be a joy for all of us to watch. I'm sure he will be a fan favourite. He showed what a player he is tonight. To get one goal and an assist on his debut is great."

"A lot can happen in just one minute of football. Even more can happen in 20. As we have just seen, that's enough time to make yourself a cult hero.

"Savio's arrival at Tottenham was shrouded in question marks. Why were Spurs willing to part with so much money for a player who managed just three goal contributions in the Premier League last season?

"Yet, the moment he stepped out onto the pitch in a white shirt, he was a livewire. Spurs fans value entertainment, and they were off their feet any time he got on the ball.

"The fact there was some end product that came with the excitement is even more important, especially for a Spurs side that have often been lacklustre in attack.

"The opponents will get tougher, and Savio will need to rise to that. However, as first outings go, having joined barely 24 hours ago, you can't ask for much more."

The key moments from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium

26: CLOSE! Charlton go cross to breaking deadlock with two near-misses.

30: SAVE! Brooks denies Gray with fingertips save.

40: GOAL! Moore opens Spurs account to give hosts lead.

45: GOAL! Solanke makes it two with a smart finish.

67: GOAL! Danso heads home with first touch to extend lead.

71: DEBUT! Savio makes his Spurs bow in place of Solanke.

82: GOAL! The moment Savio dreamt off as he scores on his debut.

85: GOAL! Savio involved again as shot deflect off Davies for five.

87: GOAL! Jones grabs consolation for Charlton from corner.

articles.title: Mbappe hat-trick fires Real Madrid to 4-1 win against Sociedad
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe hat-trick powers Real Madrid past Real Sociedad in La Liga on Jose Mourinho’s Bernabeu return.
articles.body:
Kylian Mbappe scored a brilliant hat-trick to help Real Madrid thrash Real Sociedad 4-1 in La Liga in Jose Mourinho’s first home match back at the Santiago Bernabeu as the club’s coach.

Mourinho’s Madrid made it two wins from two, with Vinicius Junior also on the scoresheet, while Jude Bellingham provided two assists as the star trio picked apart their Basque visitors.

Veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho selected the same side that snatched a late 2-1 win at Espanyol in his first match at the helm last Saturday.

Mourinho had said it would be tricky but not impossible to get the team’s three biggest names all at their best, and this match suggested he is on the right track.

Vinicius fired over, and Alex Remiro saved low at his near post from Mbappe during an open start to the game. At the other end, Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois made a smart stop from Mikel Oyarzabal.

Remiro was called into action again to deny Vinicius after Mbappe slipped in the Brazil international, while La Real’s Sergio Gomez sent a volley screaming just wide of Courtois’s far post.

Five minutes before half-time, Madrid found the breakthrough with Federico Valverde feeding Mbappe.

The French forward, top scorer in La Liga in each of the last two seasons, took a clever touch to escape his marker and buried the ball in the top corner to claim the first goal of his campaign.

However, Los Blancos could not survive to the break without conceding the equaliser against last season’s Copa del Rey winners.

Job Ochieng dallied on the ball, and his shot was blocked, but it fell nicely to Luka Sucic, who rammed home with the help of a deflection off Alvaro Carreras.

Arda Guler played in Mbappe, whom Remiro denied early in the second half, but the Spanish goalkeeper could do nothing about the former Paris Saint-Germain star’s next effort.

A neat move involving Valverde and then Bellingham led to the latter playing in Mbappe, who calmly stroked home. Madrid’s third came from Vinicius, who had been quiet until this point, and he had the tenacity of Bellingham to thank.

The England midfielder’s shot was blocked, but he refused to give up, winning the ball back in Real Sociedad’s area and putting it on a plate for Vinicius to tap home.

The Brazilian, brought to life by his goal, set up Mbappe with a perfectly weighted pass for the striker’s third, a dink over Remiro that was the pick of the goals.

Vinicius, substituted with seven minutes to go for record Madrid signing Yan Diomande, embraced Mourinho after being brought off with the job done.

Madrid’s previous campaign began to turn for the worse when Vinicius showed his anger after being replaced by Xabi Alonso during Madrid’s Clasico win over Barcelona in October, but the forward, who recently extended his club deal until 2032, was all smiles.

On Thursday, Spanish champions Barcelona host Athletic Bilbao, with new signing Rodri poised to make his debut for Hansi Flick’s side from the bench.

articles.title: Morata, muy cerca del Leganés
articles.standfirst: El delantero ha dado el OK y el Como facilitará su salida por deseo del jugador
articles.summary: El delantero ha dado el OK y el Como facilitará su salida por deseo del jugador
articles.body: Lo que hace unas horas parecía una operación casi imposible va muy en serio. Álvaro Morata ha dado el visto bueno a la posibilidad de jugar en el Leganés y su entorno está encantado con la opción de regresar a Madrid. Ahora, los clubes trabajan para cerrar una operación en la que el Como está dispuesto a facilitar la salida por deseo del propio futbolista. El presidente del club, Eduardo Cosín, y el director deportivo, Andrés Pardo, están trabajando intensamente para alcanzar un acuerdo total con el delantero. Morata sería la guinda a una profunda reconstrucción de la plantilla pepinera, que alcanzaría las 11 incorporaciones. Un mercado en el que empieza a percibirse también el cambio de propiedad, con una toma de decisiones más ágil y una dirección deportiva con mayor margen de maniobra. Por nombre, trayectoria y presente, Morata estaría entre los fichajes de mayor reputación de la historia del Leganés. Morata, sigue siendo un delantero de enorme prestigio en el fútbol europeo y viene de años siendo una pieza importante de la selección española. Si los últimos acuerdos y la burocracia no lo impiden, Andrés Pardo y el Leganés están muy cerca de apuntarse un auténtico pelotazo. Y con una curiosidad añadida: aquella broma con Morata que el club llevó a sus redes sociales hace unos cuantos años está a punto de convertirse en realidad.

images.caption: Morata, esta pretemporada con el Como. GETTY
